# dsh-plugin-brave-cdp

Drive **your own, already-running Brave** over the Chrome DevTools Protocol: the
real window, your profile, your cookies, your logins, your tabs — including the
tab you are looking at right now.

Most browser automation launches a fresh browser it owns. This one attaches to the
one you already have open, so an agent can read a login-walled page, fill a form in
a session you are signed into, or hand a task back to you mid-flight in the same
window. Nothing is scraped from a parallel profile.

Two surfaces, one implementation:

| Surface | Use it when |
|---|---|
| **DSH tools** (`brave_tabs`, `brave_goto`, …) | an agent drives the browser — schemas, rendered results, no shell quoting |
| **`brave-cdp` CLI** (shipped in this package) | a human or script drives it, or you want `jq`/`batch` pipelines |

Both call the same CDP client, so behaviour and failure messages match.

## Tools

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `brave_tabs` | list / open / focus / close tabs |
| `brave_goto` | navigate a tab (or a new one) and wait for load |
| `brave_snapshot` | interactive elements with `@eN` refs (role, name, value, href, state) |
| `brave_click` | real mouse click by `@eN` ref, CSS selector, or visible text |
| `brave_fill` | set an input / textarea / contenteditable, firing `input`/`change` |
| `brave_key` | press a key, optionally with ctrl / shift / alt / meta |
| `brave_eval` | evaluate JavaScript in the page, awaiting promises |
| `brave_wait` | wait for a selector, text, url, or document load |
| `brave_screenshot` | capture a PNG and return its path |

With no `tab` argument a tool acts on the tab the user is looking at
(`document.visibilityState === 'visible'`), and every result carries the CLI's
`tab:` header so it is clear which tab ran the call. `@eN` refs come from
`brave_snapshot` and stay valid until the page navigates.

Screenshots return a **path** rather than inline pixels: the agent reads the PNG
with whatever image-reading tool it already has, so this plugin needs no vision
pipeline of its own.

## Requirements

1. **Brave started with a CDP port.** Add the flag to the launcher's flag file
   (`~/.config/brave-flags.conf` for the Arch `brave-bin` wrapper):

   ```
   --remote-debugging-port=9222
   ```

   The flag applies at startup only, so Brave must be restarted after adding it.
   The port binds to loopback, but see [Security](#security) before enabling it.

2. **Node ≥ 22** for the CLI (it uses the built-in `fetch` and `WebSocket`; no
   dependencies). Node ≥ 22 is also required by DSH itself.

3. **DSH** with the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` peer
   packages (present in any DSH install) for the tool surface.

The CLI itself is bundled at `bin/brave-cdp.mjs`; the tools resolve it from the
package, falling back to `~/.local/bin/brave-cdp`, then to `cliPath` /
`BRAVE_CDP_CLI`.

## Install

```bash
# into a DSH profile (declares dsh.bundle.patch, so the tools row mounts itself)
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:olegedly/dsh-plugin-brave-cdp"

# or from a checkout / tarball
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-plugin-brave-cdp
```

Then confirm the endpoint is reachable:

```bash
brave-cdp status     # endpoint UP + browser version + tab count => ready
```

Standalone CLI, without DSH (not on npm yet, so install it from the repository):

```bash
npm install -g "github:olegedly/dsh-plugin-brave-cdp"   # provides `brave-cdp`
brave-cdp tabs
brave-cdp snapshot -i
brave-cdp click '@e4'
brave-cdp eval 'document.title'
brave-cdp shot page.png --full
```

## CLI

```
brave-cdp status                     endpoint, browser version, tab count
brave-cdp tabs [list]                tabs, 1-based indices, * marks the target
brave-cdp tabs new <url>             open a tab
brave-cdp tabs select <n|id|text>    focus a tab and raise its window
brave-cdp tabs close <n|id|text>     close a tab
brave-cdp open <url> [--new]         navigate (or open) and wait for load
brave-cdp back | forward | reload [--hard]
brave-cdp snapshot [scope] [-i] [--compact] [--json]
brave-cdp click <@eN|css|--text T> [--exact] [--dblclick]
brave-cdp fill <@eN|css> <text> [--append]
brave-cdp type [@eN|css] <text>
brave-cdp key <Enter|Tab|Escape|ArrowDown|...> [--ctrl --shift --alt --meta]
brave-cdp eval <js> [--file <path>|-]     evaluate JS, print JSON
brave-cdp html [css] [--text] / text [css]
brave-cdp shot [file] [--full]
brave-cdp wait <ms>|@eN|--selector S|--text T|--url U|--load
brave-cdp batch "open https://x" "wait --text Done" "shot done.png"
```

Global flags: `--tab <n|id|url-substr>`, `--json`, `--timeout <ms>`, `--port <n>`.
Env: `BRAVE_CDP_PORT` (9222), `BRAVE_CDP_HOST` (127.0.0.1), `BRAVE_CDP_TIMEOUT`.

`brave-cdp help` is the source of truth.

## Configuration

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `cliPath` | packaged `bin/brave-cdp.mjs` | CLI to invoke |
| `port` | `9222` | CDP port (must match the Brave flag) |
| `timeoutMs` | `60000` | Per-call timeout |
| `screenshotTimeoutMs` | `120000` | Screenshot timeout |

The bundled patch mounts the row as `brave-cdp`; a profile's own
`cordis.patch.yml` is applied afterwards, so override that id to change the port
or point at another CLI:

```yaml
- id: brave-cdp
  config:
    port: 9223
```

## Security

CDP is **full control of the browser**: page contents, cookies, and any session
you are logged into are readable, and it can act as you on any site. The port
binds to loopback only, which limits it to local processes — that is a boundary,
not a guarantee. Add the flag when you want an agent to drive the browser, and
remove it (and restart) when you do not.

## Development

```bash
npm run check    # node --check on the plugin and the CLI
npm test         # node --test test/ (no network, no browser needed)
```

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | the nine tools: schemas, argument mapping, result rendering |
| `bin/brave-cdp.mjs` | the CDP client — transport, target selection, DOM refs, input, screenshots |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | the bundle patch that mounts the tools row |
| `test/` | CLI behaviour and packaging invariants |

Because the CDP client lives in the CLI, the plugin is a thin adapter: one tested
code path serves both the tool surface and the shell, and the DSH host process
never imports a browser-automation dependency.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

plugins.description: Claude-Desktop-style Projects sidebar plugin for DeepSeek Harness Desktop: group conversations into projects, per-conversation working directories, drag-and-drop migration, permanent empty-conversation cleanup.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-projects

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@wxysskd/dsh-projects.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wxysskd/dsh-projects) [![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

Claude-Desktop-style **Projects** for **DSH Desktop** (the `desktop` DSH profile
only — Web and headless profiles are untouched).

The shipped DSH sidebar groups conversations by Workspace (directory). This
plugin replaces that sidebar region with a project-first browser:

- create **projects** (name, color, one or more working directories);
- every conversation lives inside a project;
- **each conversation can use a different directory**, chosen when it is
  created (or switched later through *Change working directory*), backed by the
  Host's real `workingDirectory` service — the same durable, model-visible
  mechanism as the `working_directory` tool;
- sessions outside any project stay visible under **Other conversations**,
  still grouped by Workspace, so nothing is lost;
- **empty conversations are hidden and can be deleted for real**: the Host keeps
  reusable blank Sessions from every "New Session" click (`blank: true`); only
  the empty Session that is currently open is shown. The Host also scans legacy
  Sessions whose catalog row is not marked blank but whose log contains no
  conversation events at all (only tiny header/metadata logs are inspected), so
  old "Badstuff"-style empty chats are hidden too. *View options → Delete empty
  conversations (N)* permanently removes both kinds from disk through a
  validated Host route (never touches a conversation with content; sessions
  still live in the current app run are archived and can be purged after the
  next start);
- **projects keep the workspace hierarchy**: inside a project, conversations
  stay grouped under their workspace (folder + title + count), so moving a
  workspace into a project preserves its identity instead of flattening the
  chats; workspace headers have their own `+` (new conversation directly in
  that directory — assigned to the containing project, or ungrouped under
  *Other conversations*) and `⋯` menu (new conversation, move to another
  project, rename, remove from project, delete workspace);
- pinned sessions, relative times, running/pending/unread status dots,
  archive/unarchive, rename, fork, pin and copy-ID work from the new rows.

## Install (desktop profile)

The plugin ships as a normal DSH bundle and is published on npm as
**[`@wxysskd/dsh-projects`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wxysskd/dsh-projects)**.
Three equivalent ways to install it into the **desktop** profile
(`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`):

```bash
# 1. from npm (registry install; also works from Plugins -> Add plugin)
plugin_manager install_bundle target=@wxysskd/dsh-projects@1.0.0
#   or: desktop-cli plugin --profile desktop add @wxysskd/dsh-projects@1.0.0

# 2. from the self-contained release tarball
npm run pack                                  # -> dist/wxysskd-dsh-projects-1.0.0.tgz
plugin_manager install_bundle target=/abs/path/dist/wxysskd-dsh-projects-1.0.0.tgz

# 3. source link for development (client.js edits hot-reload)
desktop-cli plugin --profile desktop add link:"$PWD"
```

The npm package contains only runtime files (`index.js`, `client.js`,
`cordis.patch.yml`, `locale/*.json`, `icon.svg`, `package.json`, `README.md`,
`LICENSE`), plus `SHA-256`/manifest in `dist/`. See
[docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md) for installation, the market index,
activation/verification and rollback details.

## Plugin market (Discover tab)

DSH has no official built-in market; the Discover tab reads index sources the
user adds. This repository publishes a format-1 index with a commit-pinned Git
install target:

```
https://aobakaolengmian.github.io/dsh-projects/market/index.json
```

Add that URL as an index source in **Plugins → Discover** and install
**Projects** from the card; the same index is readable by the `plugin_market`
tool and by any other DSH Desktop user:

![Projects in the Discover tab](docs/preview-market.png)

The market entry installs the published npm package
(`@wxysskd/dsh-projects@<version>`), the same artifact as the tarball. See
[market/README.md](market/README.md) for the format and how to regenerate it
(`npm run market`). Installing from the market still needs one app restart for
the Host row.

## Data

Project metadata is Host-owned and durable, independent of session logs:

- `$DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-projects.json` — projects, session→project
  assignments, last recorded working directory per session;
- sessions themselves stay owned by the Session Controller (nothing is
  rewritten into session logs by this plugin).

HTTP routes served from the existing DSH web server (same origin as the GUI):

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/dsh-projects/state` | complete project state |
| GET | `/dsh-projects/health` | liveness + counts |
| POST | `/dsh-projects/mutate` | `project.create`, `project.update`, `project.delete`, `session.assign` |
| POST | `/dsh-projects/cwd` | change one conversation's working directory |
| POST | `/dsh-projects/purge` | permanently remove validated empty sessions (rejects content) |
| GET | `/dsh-projects/empty-sessions` | list sessions that hold no conversation content |

POST routes require `content-type: application/json` and `x-dsh-projects: 1`
and a 64 KiB body limit.

## Build

```
npm install          # dev-only: esbuild, react, react-dom, playwright
node scripts/build.mjs   # src/client/* -> client.js (committed artifact)
npm run pack             # build + dist/<name>-<version>.tgz + SHA-256 + manifest
node harness/build.mjs   # mock harness bundle
node harness/shoot.mjs   # screenshots -> harness/shots/
npm test                 # host/model tests (node --test)
```

## Design notes

- The browser entry registers into the shipped `sidebar.workspaces` single slot
  at `priority: -1`, shadowing `ui-workspace`'s browser. The shipped entry stays
  registered underneath: if our component crashes, its entry is abdicated and
  the original sidebar comes back.
- The client bundle imports only `react` / `react-dom` / `react/jsx-runtime`
  from the shell's shared module table and uses `ctx` services for everything
  else (`sessions`, `workspaces`, `uiWorkspace`, `locale`, `slots`).
- Styles use `--dsw-*` theme tokens; literals are limited to project accent
  artwork. All classes are prefixed `pj-`.

## Moving workspaces and conversations between projects

Everything can be migrated without deleting or recreating sessions, through the
project metadata only (session logs are never touched):

- **Drag a conversation row** onto any project section → the session is assigned
  to that project (drag it onto *Other conversations* to remove it from its
  project).
- **Drag a workspace group header** (under *Other conversations*) onto any
  project section → the directory moves into that project (removed from any
  other project's directory list, never duplicated) and every conversation in
  that directory is assigned to it. While dragging, every project shows a
  dashed drop outline and the hovered target is highlighted.
- **Menu path** (same result without dragging):
  - workspace group `⋯` → *Move workspace to project* → pick the target;
  - project `⋯` → *Move working directory to another project…* → pick the
    directory → pick the target project (or *Remove from project (back to Other
    conversations)*);
  - conversation `⋯` → *Move to project* → pick the target (or *No project*).

Moving a directory between projects also makes future sessions created in that
directory (including the shipped Cmd+N flow) land in the target project, and the
project keeps the workspace title as a nested folder group.

Workspace headers (both inside projects and under *Other conversations*) expose
their own menu: **Rename workspace…**, **Move workspace to project**, **Remove
from project** and **Delete workspace**. Deleting a workspace removes only its
registration, puts its conversations back under *Other conversations*, and never
deletes a conversation.

## Compatibility with other sidebar plugins

The installed sidebar-touching pl

plugins.description: 给 DSH Desktop 的鲸鱼壁纸插件：一片会游动的海铺在界面背后，控制台 20 项实时可调
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-whale-pond 🐋

> 一只在深海里慢慢游的鲸鱼，把它的自留地铺在 **DSH** 的 Web 界面背后（桌面端窗口，或浏览器里打开的 `dsh web`）。
> 纯视觉背景插件：**不拦鼠标、不抢键盘、不碰任何业务代码**。

[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/wenwubei5/dsh-whale-pond?color=2b6cb0)](https://github.com/wenwubei5/dsh-whale-pond/releases/latest)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)
[![DSH Desktop](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH%20Desktop-0.2.0--rc.2-1f2937)](https://github.com/wenwubei5/dsh-whale-pond)


## 它是什么

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）的 Web 界面背后本来是一块不透明背景。这个插件在 `z-index:-1` 挂一张
`position:fixed` 的全屏 canvas，再把界面自己的背景 token 调成半透明玻璃 —— 于是海、光点、水母、
鲸鱼就从界面底下透出来了：

- 默认 **400 颗光点**在海里飘（可拉到 2100），鲸鱼游过去把它们吃掉，头上飘一行 `-1 token`
- 鼠标是一盏**提灯**，带着洋流把光点往鲸鱼嘴边赶
- 右下角有个**发射区**：鼠标进圈，圈里的光点和鲸鱼一起被甩出去（最远约 4 倍圈直径）
- 右上角齿轮 ⚙ 是**控制台**：12 个滑杆 + 7 个开关 + 1 个下拉 + 1 个词库框 + 5 个按钮，改完立刻变
- 齿轮左边还有一个 **■ / ▶ 一键停用**：动画停、玻璃撤掉、界面回到原样，设置会记住
- **看海模式**：一键全屏屏保（盖住界面文字，专心看鲸鱼吃光点），或弹出的可拖动 / 可缩放小窗（浮在界面上摸鱼）；点画面或按 Esc 退出
- **五种运动方式**（漂移 / 飘落 / 上浮 / 洋流 / 漩涡）+ **呼吸灯**，和鼠标吸引、发射台叠加生效
- 深浅色主题自动跟随；`prefers-reduced-motion` 时跑 120 帧后定格；页面隐藏时暂停


## 安装

前提：**页面必须是 DSH 自己的 Web 界面** —— 桌面端窗口，或者用 `dsh web` 起在浏览器里打开，两者都行
（见下面「在浏览器里用」）。插件走的是 DSH 的客户端插件机制（`window.__ModuleLoader__`），所以不能当普通
`<script>` 塞进别的网页；但它**不是 Electron 专属**，Chromium 内核的浏览器里实测正常。
仓库里已经带了生成好的 `lib/client.js`，**装的时候不需要 Node、不需要 Python、不需要构建**。

### 方式 A：一条命令从 GitHub 直装（推荐）

```bash
# 1) 先确认活动 profile —— 这个文件里 "active" 那一项就是（常见 desktop / web）
cat "$APPDATA/DSH Desktop/profile-selection"

# 2) 用桌面端自带的 CLI，把 GitHub 上的包直接装进 profile（dsh 一般不在 PATH 里）
DSH="/c/Program Files/DSH Desktop"        # 换成你自己的安装目录
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 DSH_HOME="$HOME/.dsh" "$DSH/DSH Desktop.exe" \
  --expose-internals "$DSH/resources/app/lib/desktop-cli.js" \
  plugin --profile desktop add "github:wenwubei5/dsh-whale-pond"
```

`plugin add` 后面的参数是**原样转给 pnpm** 的，所以三种写法都行：

| 写法 | 例子 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub 简写 | `github:wenwubei5/dsh-whale-pond` | 装当前 main 的最新提交 |
| git URL | `git+https://github.com/wenwubei5/dsh-whale-pond.git` | 同上，可加 `#v1.0.0` 钉版本 |
| 本地目录 | `"D:/code/dsh-whale-pond"` | 装成 `link:`，改源码刷新即生效 |

### 方式 B：先 clone 再装（想改源码用这个）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/wenwubei5/dsh-whale-pond.git "D:/code/dsh-whale-pond"
# 然后照上面第 2 步，最后一段换成：
#   plugin --profile desktop add "D:/code/dsh-whale-pond"
```

改完 `src/whale_pond.html` 或 `src/whale_panel.js` 后跑 `python build/build.py` 重新生成
`lib/client.js`（只要 Python 3 + 标准库，没有第三方依赖）。

**新增插件包必须重启一次 DSH**（客户端入口要重新扫描）。之后再改代码就只要刷新页面（Ctrl+R）。
从 GitHub 装的是**中性默认词**版本；你自己的词库存在 `localStorage`，不受影响。

### 方式 C：下载 zip（离线 / 机器上没有 git）

到 [Releases](https://github.com/wenwubei5/dsh-whale-pond/releases/latest) 下载 `dsh-whale-pond-1.2.0.zip`
（约 50 KB，里面是 `package.json` + `lib/` + `cordis.patch.yml` + `README.md` + `LICENSE`），
解压出 `dsh-whale-pond/`，再把上面的命令最后一段换成那个目录：

```bash
... plugin --profile desktop add "D:/下载/dsh-whale-pond"
```

zip 里的 `lib/client.js` 就是生成好的产物（59,680 B），解压即可用，不需要构建。

卸载：把上面的 `add` 换成 `remove`。

### 在浏览器里用（不打开桌面端窗口）

插件跑在 DSH 的 Web 界面里，所以只要页面是 DSH 提供的，用浏览器打开效果完全一样。桌面端自带的 CLI 就能起
一个纯 Web 实例：

```bash
DSH="/c/Program Files/DSH Desktop"          # 换成你自己的安装目录
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 DSH_HOME="$HOME/.dsh" "$DSH/DSH Desktop.exe" \
  --expose-internals "$DSH/resources/app/lib/desktop-cli.js" \
  --profile web --port 4407 --no-open
```

它会打印一行 `http://127.0.0.1:4407/?token=…`，复制到 Chrome / Edge 里打开就有鲸鱼、光点和控制台。
**插件要装进提供这个页面的那个 profile** —— 上面安装命令里的 `--profile desktop` 换成 `--profile web` 即可。

两点要知道：

- 桌面端窗口自己那个端口（默认 `43120`）是给 Electron 渲染进程用的：浏览器直接开会被 DSH 的鉴权挡住（401），
  插件路由还带 `x-dsh-desktop-renderer` 头校验。这是宿主自己的限制，跟插件无关。
- 实测用的是 Chromium 内核（Chrome / Edge）；Firefox / Safari 没测，理论上没问题（只用到 canvas 2D、CSS 变量和 localStorage）。

## 控制台

界面右上角的小齿轮 ⚙（悬停变亮）点开就是控制台，拖动即时生效、不用刷新。
设置存在 `localStorage['whale-pond-settings-v1']`（词库单独一个键），面板底部「恢复默认（词库保留）」一键回默认。

| 分组 | 控件 | 默认 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 开关 | 启用壁纸 ☑（和右上角 ■ / ▶ 等价） | 开 |
| 看海 | 全屏屏保 · 小窗摸鱼 · 回到壁纸（三个按钮，当前生效那个亮橙） | 壁纸模式 |
| 界面 | 面板不透明度 · 画布亮度 | 0.34 · 1.6 |
| 海 | 光点数量 · 光点速度 | 400 · 1.0 |
| 鼠标（提灯） | 洋流吸引光点 ☑ · 吸引半径 · 吸引强度 · 显示吸引范围光环 ☑ | 340px · 1.0 |
| 吃光点 | 飘字「-1 token」☑ · 飘字「吃掉「词」」☑ | 都开 |
| 词库 | 一行一个词，最多 200 个 / 每个 24 字，改一下存一下 | 内建 10 个词 |
| 右下角发射台 | 启用发射台 ☑ · 圈半径 · 距右下角 · 弹射力度 | 170px · 132px · 4.0 |
| 光点运动 | 运动方式 · 运动强度 · 呼吸灯 ☐ · 呼吸快慢 | 漂移 · 1.0 · 关 · 1.0 |
| 性能 | 内部清晰度 · 运行状态（只读） | 1.0 |

## 停用 / 恢复

要认真工作、不想再看海的时候，点右上角齿轮左边那个 **■** 就停（停用后按钮变成 **▶**、亮橙色，再点一下回来）；
也可以打开控制台，最上面「开关」组里取消「启用壁纸」。两条路等价，状态存在 localStorage，**刷新页面依然是停的**。

它是真停，不是把画布藏起来：

- `cancelAnimationFrame` 停掉动画，canvas `display:none`；
- 120ms 吃光点、12s 造带词光点两个定时器和补货入口都提前返回；
- 宿主那层玻璃**整份撤掉**（`tokens.reset()`：body 的 `background:transparent !important` 与 8 个 `--dsw-alias-bg-*` 覆盖全部移除），界面回到原本不透明的深色；
- 齿轮与面板留着当入口（齿轮降到 0.3 透明度），控制台「运行状态」会写「已停用 · 动画停、玻璃已撤」。

恢复时按 `tokens.apply()` → `run()` → 补齐光点数 的顺序来，不会出现「海回来了但界面还是实心」的中间态。
真页面实测：停用前 1.2 秒画 28,263 个弧，停用后同一窗口 **0** 个；禁缓存重载后仍 `display:none` / 0 弧，勾回来立刻恢复到 27,287 个弧。

## 看海：全屏屏保 · 小窗摸鱼

控制台最上面「看海」组里三个按钮（别和齿轮左边那个 ■ / ▶ 停用混起来）：

- **全屏屏保** —— 整片海铺满窗口，把界面文字全盖住，鲸鱼和光点在整屏里游。底部会浮出一条
  「点击画面或按 Esc 退出」的胶囊提示，5 秒后自己淡出。副屏上放着纯看很合适。
- **小窗摸鱼** —— 一个约 280×180 的圆角小海窗浮在右下角，界面照常能点能用；拖窗内任意处移动，
  拖右下角手柄缩放（280×180 ~ 560×347）。窗口一直被夹在视口里，不会拖丢。
- **回到壁纸** —— 回到正常的「铺满整个界面背后」模式。

三种模式互斥，当前生效的按钮亮橙色。这个**模式本身不记忆**：刷新页面就回到壁纸模式
（「启用壁纸」那个停用开关倒是会记住）。

实现上三件事值得说：

- 看海时画布**离开 `z-index:-1`**：小窗 `2147482990`、全屏 `2147483002`（压在界面上，也压住自己的齿轮和面板），
  提示条 `2147483003`。回壁纸再回到 `-1` 并恢复 `pointer-events:none`。
- 进看海先把玻璃背景**整份撤掉**（`tokens.reset()`），否则小窗后面还是透的、看不清；回壁纸且没停用时再 `tokens.apply()`。
- 画布尺寸一变就按比例**重排光点**（`rebaseMotes`：坐标等比缩放 + 绕屏回绕），不会有光点被甩到画布外；
  小窗里鼠标坐标要减去窗口偏移，提灯才会指哪儿亮哪儿。

真页面实测（754×440 视口）：全屏 canvas `rect [0,0,754,440]`、`z-index 2147483002`、界面 token 全空（玻璃撤净）；
小窗 `z-index 2147482990`、拖动 -60/+40 跟手、缩放 280×180 → 360×240、手柄跟着走；Esc 退出后宿主收到的 Escape 次数 **0**
（不会顺手取消掉你正在生成的回答）；停用壁纸时若正在看海，会自动回到壁纸并 `display:none`。

## 实现要点（这些坑都踩过）

- **canvas 要 `z-index:-1`，但光这样是看不见的**：body 自己的不透明背景画在负 z-index 后代之上，
  样式表压不住主题规则 —— 必须 `document.body.style.setProperty("background","transparent","important")`（inline + important 实测必胜）。
- **设计 token 定义在 body 上、不在 html 上**：往 `documentElement` 写等于白写。token 覆盖成半透明后，
  界面自己就变玻璃了（透明度表在 `lib/client.js` 的 `TOKENS`）。
- **背景要烘焙**：海面渐变 + 暗角很贵，改成离屏 canvas 各烘一次（背景 1/4 分辨率、暗角只在建立或改尺寸时烘），
  每秒的离屏重绘像素量从 3.3M 降到 254K。
- **光点要批量画**：按类型分 4 桶、每桶一次 `fill()`；呼吸灯再按 3 档亮度分桶（每帧 fill 29 → 45，仍然不掉帧）。
- **「跟手」得用阻尼弹簧 + 距离比例力**：把弹簧力写成单位向量会让拉力弱约 100 倍，光点「越赶越散」。
- **发射出去的光点要免疫鼠标吸引**（`if(lamp.on && !(m.lz>0))`），否则会被鼠标自己拽回来、飞不远。
- **帧门 `if(dt < 24) return;` + `document.hidden` 暂停 + DPR ≤ 1.5 + 32fps 上限**，4K 屏也稳。
- **停用要做成「可逆的拆除」**：rAF 只留一个入口（`run()`），停时 `cancelAnimationFrame` 并把 `running` 置假；画布 `display:none` 比停止绘制更彻底（连合成都不做）；玻璃背景必须 `tokens.reset()` 逐个 `removeProperty`，只覆盖不撤会永远留着半透明。
- **看海时的 Esc 必须拦在捕获阶段**：面板的 keydown 监听挂在 `document` 捕获阶段（第三参 `true`），看海模式下 `preventDefault + stopPropagation` 再退出，宿主收不到这次 Esc（DSH 里 Esc = 取消生成）；面板关着时不能拦，得让它照常穿透。
- **小窗要整只夹在视口里**（`Math.max(4, Math.min(vh - h - 4, y))`），提示条贴底时改挂到小窗上方，否则固定挂在下方会被视口切掉、截图里根本看不见。

## 改它

```
src/whale_pond.html   # 原版海洋小游戏 —— 物理与绘制的来源（build.py 按行号引用它）
src/whale_panel.js    # 控制台（面板）源码
build/build.py        # 生成器：按行号剪裁 src/whale_pond.html + 注入补丁 → lib/client.js
lib/client.js         # 生成产物（已提交，装完即用，不需要构建工具）
test/harness.html     # 离线夹具：假 __ModuleLoader__ + 手动 rAF 泵，无头浏览器 3 秒跑完
test/probes/*.js      # 真页面 CDP 探针（看海模式 / 停用开关 / 运动方式 / 控制台 / 词库 / 发射区 / 越界值 / 全控件扫描）
```

重建（会重写 `lib/client.js`、`cordis.patch.yml`、`package.json`）：

```bash
python build/build.py
node --check lib/client.js
```

### 离线夹具（不用起 DSH）

```bash
msedge --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --virtual-time-budget=300000 \
  --dump-dom "file:///$(pwd)/test/harness.html" | grep -o 'RESULT {.*}'
```

夹具返回一大坨 JSON：每帧 `arc` 调用数、光点数量、控制台 20 个控件的读数、
五种运动方式的平均位移（最近邻匹配）、呼吸灯的半径分布、离屏烘焙成本，
以及两个历史 bug 的回归项（面板开着时 Esc 不穿透、localStorage 越界值自动夹紧）。

### 真页面探针

先起一个测试用的 DSH 实例，再用无头 Edge 连上去：

```bash
node test/front.mjs 4406                        # 让标签页前台化（否则 rAF 一帧不发）
node test/cdp.mjs test/probes/motion.js shot.png 4406
```

`test/cdp.mjs <探针.js> <截图.png|""> <url 子串>`，截图参数传空串就只求值。

## English

A purely visual wallpaper plugin for **DSH Desktop**: a whale, drifting motes and jellyfish are
drawn on a fixed `z-index:-1` canvas behind the web

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-file-reference

**右键**一键引用：把侧栏「工作区文件」树里的文件/文件夹、或消息里**已交付的文件卡片**，以原生 `@路径` 引用 chip 插进当前会话输入框。

DeepSeek Harness 里想引用一个文件，只能手打 `@` 再一层层找；而侧栏文件树只有**左键**一个手势（点文件=打开预览、点目录=展开），交付文件卡片也没有引用入口。本插件补上**右键**这一步，走的是宿主自己的引用通道，不自造协议。

## 效果

在右侧栏「工作区文件」面板里**右键**任意文件或文件夹行，或者在消息里**右键已交付的文件卡片**（例如收尾回复下方的 `combo_index.html` 卡片）：

| 菜单项 | 行为 |
|---|---|
| **引用到会话** | 把该条目以 `@路径` chip 插入当前会话输入框——与把文件拖进输入框**同一条宿主通道**，插入的是真正的引用 chip，发送时宿主按文件引用解析 |
| **复制引用文本** | 把 `@路径` 文本写入剪贴板 |

- 路径自动折算成相对当前会话工作区的相对路径；含空格的路径自动加引号（`@"my dir/readme.md"`）；目录尾随 `/`。
- 插入成功自动聚焦输入框；会话未挂载、正在发送或输入框拒绝插入时**给出提示**，不静默失败。
- 命中不到路径时**不拦截右键**，浏览器的默认行为照常。
- 菜单样式全取宿主主题令牌，亮暗主题跟随；点击别处、Esc、滚动、窗口失焦自动关闭。
- 中英双语，跟随宿主语言。

## 安装

> **发布状态**：本插件目前只在 GitHub 发布，**尚未发布到 npm**。下面标注「npm 未发布」的写法暂不可用，等发布后再用。

### 方式一 · 插件页添加（桌面版用户，推荐）

DSH 桌面版：打开侧边栏**插件**页 → **添加插件** → 粘贴下面一行 → 装完点**启用** → 按提示重启或刷新。

```
https://github.com/dyhdesu/dsh-file-reference
```

### 方式二 · 命令行（web / headless profile）

```
dsh plugin --profile web add github:dyhdesu/dsh-file-reference
```

装完重启 `dsh web`，浏览器硬刷新。

npm 发布后可直接用包名安装（**当前 npm 未发布，此条暂不可用**）：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-file-reference
```

### 方式三 · 本地目录接线（开发用）

`desktop` profile 由 Electron 应用独占管理，官方 CLI 会拒绝直接写入（`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`）。自己开发时走手动接线：

```sh
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop
```

在该目录的 `package.json` 里，`dependencies` 增加一条指向本目录的 `file:` 依赖，并在 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里追加 `"dsh-file-reference"`；然后在同目录执行安装并重启桌面版。

```
pnpm install
```

改完源码后同步安装副本，client 半区刷新页面即生效：

```
rsync -a --delete src/ ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-file-reference/src/
```

## 原理

- 两个右键表面都由一个纯逻辑函数 `contextTarget()` 判定，命中才拦截：
  - **侧栏文件树行**：官方文件树（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-files`）的行节点带 `data-files-entry="file|directory"` 与 `data-files-path="绝对路径"`，树根带 `data-files-root`；官方树本身没有任何右键处理，这块手势是空的。
  - **交付文件卡片**：官方交付卡片（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-deliverables`）是 `div[data-presented-file]`，其中**只作标记、不带路径**；绝对路径在卡片内**首个带 `title` 的节点**（预览按钮，官方 `resolveWorkspacePath(cwd, file.path)`）上。该 `title` 是非 i18n 的，但属于官方**内部实现**而非公开契约——因此插件按**文档顺序**取第一个非空 `title`，取不到就完全不拦截右键。卡片位于正文中，归属即当前会话，无需树根纠偏。
- 插入走宿主 `conversation` 服务的 `input.shell(sessionId).addFiles([reference], [])`，即 `SessionInputShell.addFiles`——官方给引用 chip 留的程序化入口（内部走 `draftEditor.insertFileReferences`）；chip 形态 `{source:'reference', ref, label, appearance, clipboardText}` 与官方 `@` 菜单、拖文件进输入框**完全一致**，不是自造协议。
- 当前会话由 `uiSession.current.value.key` 提供；多会话时按文件树根路径与会话 `cwd` 比对纠偏，避免把引用插进别的会话。
- 与官方 `@` 引用语义对齐：引用只携带**路径**，不读取也不附带文件内容（官方 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-file-reference` 明文规定「选中候选绝不读取或附带文件内容」），模型要看内容必须自己调文件系统工具。
- **纯前端插件**：host 半区为空操作（`export function apply() {}`），不碰宿主源码、不注册路由、不改配置，装卸无残留；HMR 重评估时先拆上一代句柄（监听器、菜单、代际槽）。

## 兼容性

- 在 **DSH 0.2.1-rc.2**（macOS 桌面版）上开发与验证。
- **Windows**：路径处理对齐官方文件树的混合分隔符契约（官方 `childPath` 以 `/` 拼接、宿主解析混合分隔符），盘符与 UNC 形态按大小写不敏感比对，POSIX 形态仍严格区分大小写。盘符、反斜杠与混合分隔符、盘符大小写差异、UNC 四种形态均有单元测试覆盖；**尚未在 Windows 实机验收**。
- 依赖官方文件树的行属性契约（`data-files-entry` / `data-files-path` / `data-files-root`）、交付卡片的 `data-presented-file` 标记与其预览按钮的 `title`、以及 `SessionInputShell.addFiles`。官方若改动这三处，插件需要跟进；已做降级：服务缺失、结构不匹配或取不到路径时既不抛异常，也不拦截右键。
- 输入框中的引用 chip 形态与官方 `@` 菜单、拖拽入文件一致，因此引用在草稿恢复、跨工作区切换等场景下与官方行为一致。

## 已知局限

- 一次只处理单行：暂不支持多选批量引用。
- 右键覆盖侧栏文件树行与**交付文件卡片**两处；消息里已渲染的 `@` 引用 chip、改动文件卡片的行、收尾正文的行内文件链接暂不在范围内。
- 交付卡片依赖官方 `title` 这个内部实现细节；官方改版后可能失效（表现为右键不再弹菜单，不影响其它功能）。
- 目录引用只插入 `@目录/`，不展开目录内容（官方 `@` 菜单的 Tab 下钻能力未复刻）。
- 引用 chip 插入需要会话已挂载且输入框可编辑；发送中会被宿主拒绝并提示。

## 开发与测试

```sh
npm test
```

45 项用例覆盖：路径归一化与 `@` 语法（含空格引号、目录尾斜杠、控制字符拒绝）、**Windows 形态**（盘符、反斜杠与混合分隔符、盘符大小写差异、UNC、根前缀兄弟目录不误判）、chip 载荷构造、会话归属判定、**右键命中判定**（树行/交付卡片/树外与无 title 不拦截）、菜单生命周期与拆卸、服务全缺时的降级，以及 `src/client.js` 内联逻辑段与 `src/logic.mjs` 的**逐字同源校验**（防止两侧逻辑漂移）。

## 许可

MIT © 2026 dyhdesu

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-dashboard

DeepSeek Harness（DSH）Web UI 侧边栏插件：在左侧新增「项目看板」，把任务进度、下载/解压、模型训练、测试结果和 GPU 状态集中到一个紧凑面板。

## 功能

- **紧凑单面板**：顶部任务进度卡 + 任务 / 下载 / 训练 / 测试 / 传输五个页签，列表在面板内滚动。
- **任务进度**：读取工作区任务计划，结合服务器产物与运行中的进程推断每项任务的状态、进度和下一步（转换、校验、训练、评测进程会自动识别）。
- **下载与解压**：本地下载目录与远端 raw 目录；归档显示已解压体积/文件数，解压中显示百分比和当前第几个压缩包。
- **模型训练**：最近的训练产物；GPU 支持**本机 + 多台远端**（`remoteAliases`），每个来源一组，显示利用率、显存、温度、功耗、风扇、频率、驱动、占用进程，以及该机器的 CPU / 内存 / load；每张卡带一条最近约 30 个采样的利用率迷你趋势线。
- **测试信息**：pytest 历史（每个 run 目录取最新一份日志）、评测指标和结果目录。
- **传输**：新增「传输」页签，显示 dsh-ssh 文件传输的**方向（↑ 上传 / ↓ 下载）、阶段（接收/发送）、已传输字节、速率、已用时间**和最近完成记录，并可一键清空已完成；同时聚合服务器上的 `scp` / `rsync` / `sftp` 进程并解析其方向。传输页签每 2 秒单独轮询，不拖慢主快照。
- **点击查看详情**：点击任意条目打开右侧详情抽屉——测试显示 pytest 日志末尾，训练显示产物列表/指标/日志末尾，下载显示大小与解压明细，传输显示方向/阶段/速率/路径；详情里的路径可一键复制，行尾的复制图标仍可直接复制完整路径。
- 支持来源筛选（全部/本地/服务器）和名称/路径搜索；当前页签与来源会记住；服务端不可用时不影响本地数据。

远程数据通过 `dsh-ssh` 的 loopback exec 路由只读采集，不复制或存储 SSH 凭据；未安装 `dsh-ssh` 时插件仍可只展示本地工作区。

## 安装

1. 克隆仓库；
2. 在 DSH 插件管理页安装本目录，或使用 `plugin_manager install_bundle` 指向克隆目录的绝对路径；
3. 首次安装后重启 DSH。之后修改文件可以在插件管理页把 bundle 关一次再开，触发热重载，无需重启。

可选依赖：已安装并配置主机别名的 `dsh-ssh`（用于远程数据与 GPU）。

## 配置

在 `cordis.patch.yml` 的插件行里配置：

```yaml
config:
  localRoot: '/path/to/workspace'   # 要扫描的本地工作区
  remoteAlias: 'my-ssh-host'        # 主 dsh-ssh 主机别名；留空则只扫描本地
  remoteAliases:                    # 可选：额外的 GPU/主机监控目标（同样经 dsh-ssh）
    - 'gpu-host-2'
  remoteRoots:
    downloadRoot: '/data/downloads'
    trainingRoot: '/data/runs'
    logRoot: '/data/logs'
  refreshSeconds: 20                # 快照缓存时间
```

`remoteAlias` 同时是项目数据（下载/训练/测试/任务）的主机来源；`remoteAliases` 里的额外主机只聚合 GPU 与主机资源。可选键：`showLocal`、`showRemote`（布尔）。

仓库里的 `cordis.patch.yml` 只保留空配置；本机实际使用的路径、SSH 别名等建议写在 **profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`** 覆盖层（同 id 覆盖），这样仓库里不会出现个人路径。

## 接口

- `GET /api/dino-dashboard/state`：当前快照（过期则重建）
- `GET /api/dino-dashboard/transfers`：轻量传输状态（2 秒轮询，不触发 SSH 扫描）
- `GET /api/dino-dashboard/detail?source=local|remote&path=...&kind=...`：条目详情（本地读文件末尾/目录；远端经 dsh-ssh 读取）
- `POST /api/dino-dashboard/refresh`：强制重建

两个接口都只接受 loopback 请求，且只返回只读状态信息。

## 开发

```
package.json         # bundle patch + dsh.client（platform web）
cordis.patch.yml     # Host 行与配置
index.js             # Host：本地扫描、远程探测、路由
client.js            # Client：侧边栏入口与看板页面
locale/{zh,en}.json  # 插件管理页标题/描述
icon.svg             # 图标
```

安装后修改文件，重新安装或对 bundle 做一次「关→开」即可热重载。

DSH Mobile — DeepSeek Harness Remote

An open-source Android companion that puts your DeepSeek Harness in your pocket.
Drive sessions, review plans and goals, answer approvals and questions, and get notified when the harness finishes — from your phone, over your network or a relay.

English · 中文 · हिन्दी · Español · Français · ไทย

DSH Mobile is an **unofficial companion app** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (MIT). It mirrors the web GUI feature for feature and uses the harness's own visual language. Android only, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose. Its companion on the other end is [**dsh-relay**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-relay), a harness plugin that adds the authentication layer the harness says it lacks, so this app can reach a harness with a real credential and a pinned key instead of an open port. See [Relay](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Relay). **[dshm.zyphite.com](https://dshm.zyphite.com)** is the project site: what the app is, what it looks like, and how to get it running, on one page. Drafts are kept per host and session. - Workspace panels — tabbed text, Markdown, image, PDF and isolated HTML previews; native terminal controls with a bundled xterm renderer; archived-session restore in Settings. - Message feedback — confirmed ratings and retraction, with version-conflict handling. - Slash commands and skills — typing `/` lists the session's commands and skills above the composer. The composer checks a `/` line against the session's own command catalog and runs it through the harness's command gateway. Anything the catalog does not claim is sent as a prompt, which is how skills get invoked. With the dsh-rewind plugin on the host, `/rewind` opens a picker. - Everything the GUI does — goals (phases, rounds, pause/resume/edit), plan mode and plan review, permission approvals, user questions, todo dock, subagents (catalog, follow-ups, interrupt), background jobs, workflow runs, skills, model selection, agent presets, session search, trajectory ledger, session export, message feedback. - Notifications — turn complete, goal complete or blocked, review or question waiting for you. A foreground service keeps the connection alive in the background. - Harness look — the exact DeepSeek Harness design tokens (colors, type, radii, disclosure rows, shimmer, ink buttons), with light, dark and system themes. - 11 languages — English, 中文, हिन्दी, Español, Français, العربية, বাংলা, Português, Русский, اردو, ไทย (RTL aware). ### Added in 0.15.0 - A Check now button for updates in Settings > About. The automatic check also runs again when you come back to the app after a few hours. - Workspace links in replies drawn as file and folder pills; a folder opens in Files. - A redesigned Details panel, Workspace screen and Settings, with archived sessions on a tab of their own. ### Added in 0.14.0 - A `/` menu above the composer with the session's commands and skills. - A picker for the dsh-rewind plugin's `/rewind` and `/undo` that asks for confirmation before it restores files. The transcript hides what a rewind withdrew and marks the cut. ### Added in 0.13.0 - Automation catalog, timing edits, delivery history and session shortcuts. - Plugin installation, updates, toggles, removal, progress and recovery. Create plugin stages an unsent draft with the Creator preset when the host offers it. - Timed questions, continued replies, saved answer drafts and reopenable plans. - Draft text and file, folder and session references saved across app restarts. - Model search, YAML document properties and multiline goal editing. - Reverse-proxy path support and tool argument previews while the model is writing. ## Requirements - Android 8.0+ (minSdk 26). - A running [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) at `0.2.1-alpha.2`, the protocol baseline for DSH Mobile `0.16.0`. Existing protocol fallbacks remain for `0.2.0-rc.1`, `0.1.7-rc.x` and `0.1.6-alpha.x`; new management features need host support. See [compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) and the [0.13.0 validation status](docs/VALIDATION-0.13.0.md) for what has been checked on this baseline. ## Quick start 1. Install the latest APK from [Releases](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/releases/latest). 2. Open the app and choose how to connect. plugins.description: Ollama Cloud for DeepSeek Harness: one API key, auto-pulled model catalog, real thinking levels, hosted web tools, and 5h/7d quota + token usage UI
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-ollama-cloud

Ollama Cloud for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`). One API
key; no local Ollama install.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

![Sidebar quota chip](docs/ui-main.png)

## Install

```sh
# desktop app profile and/or web profile
dsh plugin --profile desktop add git:github.com/pei-lin-001/dsh-ollama-cloud
dsh plugin --profile web add git:github.com/pei-lin-001/dsh-ollama-cloud
```

Open **Settings → Ollama Cloud**, paste a key from
[ollama.com/settings/keys](https://ollama.com/settings/keys), and press **保存并同步** (save and
sync). The key goes into the credentials service (`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`) and never reaches
the browser. The catalog is written to the `llm-pi-ai` settings section as route `ollama-cloud`, and
the models appear in the picker.

`OLLAMA_API_KEY` in the process environment also works. It shadows a stored key, and the credentials
service then refuses writes.

Development checkout:

```sh
git clone git@github.com:pei-lin-001/dsh-ollama-cloud.git ~/Dev/dsh-ollama-cloud
cd ~/Dev/dsh-ollama-cloud && dsh plugin --profile web add link:$PWD
./scripts/link-peers.sh   # schemastery, dsh-credentials, dsh-settings, dsh-tools
```

A linked package resolves peers from its own `node_modules`, which is why the last step exists.

## What it does

On boot, on credential change, and on demand, the plugin pulls the account's catalog and writes it as
an `llm-pi-ai` route: `GET /v1/models` for the ids, then one `POST /api/show` per model. Chat, tools,
vision and thinking are served by `dsh-llm-pi-ai` (`api: openai-completions`,
`baseURL: https://ollama.com/v1`); the plugin supplies the catalog and the credential, and
`dsh-llm-pi-ai` does the transport.

Model entries come from `/api/show`:

- `capabilities` decides which models get tools, vision and a thinking set. Models without `tools`
  are skipped unless `includeNonToolModels` is on.
- `<arch>.context_length` becomes `contextWindow`.
- `thinking.values` becomes `reasoningEfforts`. `false` maps to `off: 'none'`, since sending nothing
  would fall back to the model default (usually on). `true` maps to a single `medium` level. Graded
  names map one-to-one, so a model advertising both `xhigh` and `max` offers both.

The list replaces the route's models, and an unchanged section is not rewritten.

Two tools come with it: `ollama_web_search` and `ollama_web_fetch` call `/api/web_search` and
`/api/web_fetch` with the same key.

Quota and usage come from `GET /api/balance` (5h session, 7d weekly) and `GET /api/usage`. A current
plan reports tokens and cost there; a legacy plan reports requests only. For legacy plans the plugin
taps the `usage` chunk its own requests emit through `llm/stream`, counts input/cached/output per
model in hourly buckets, keeps 30 days in `$DSH_HOME/ollama-cloud-usage.json`, and aligns the totals
with the reset times the balance reports. Other clients' traffic stays invisible to that meter, so
server numbers win when they exist.

Every history image is re-sent on every step, and Ollama Cloud rejects an oversized request at the
gateway before the model runs (413, around 12 MB observed). The plugin keeps image base64 under 6 MiB:
on `0.2.x` it writes `maxRequestImageBytes` into the route, so the adapter stops at the bound and the
harness offloads the oldest images and retries with placeholders; on `0.1.0-rc.x`, whose adapter has
no such bound, the plugin drops the oldest images from the outgoing request itself. Text is not part
of that budget.

## UI

![Settings: connection and plan quota](docs/ui-settings-quota.png)

![Settings: usage charts and per-model table](docs/ui-settings-usage.png)

The settings page has four parts: connection, quota bars, charts, per-model table. The 24h chart is
hourly requests. The 7d chart switches between requests and tokens, because requests are the series
every plan returns. The sidebar footer shows both quota windows. UI copy is Chinese.

## Configuration

Entry config is the `ollama-cloud` settings section; override it in the profile patch:

```yaml
- id: ollama-cloud
  config:
    provider: ollama-cloud        # llm-pi-ai route name
    displayName: Ollama Cloud
    apiKeyRef: OLLAMA_API_KEY     # credential reference, never the secret
    baseURL: https://ollama.com
    syncOnStart: true             # pull the catalog on boot
    includeNonToolModels: false   # keep tool-less models out of the picker
    webTools: true                # register ollama_web_search / ollama_web_fetch
    maxOutputChars: 20000         # per ollama_web_fetch result
    usageCacheSeconds: 120        # /api/balance + /api/usage cache
    maxRequestImageBytes: 6291456 # base64 image budget per request; 0 = adapter default
```

A model's `contextWindow` comes from `/api/show`. The composer's 上下文 chip beside the model button
overrides it for the selected model only; the choice is kept in `$DSH_HOME/ollama-cloud-context.json`
and layered on top of every catalog sync. Resetting restores the reported value.

## Command and routes

`/ollama-cloud [status|sync|usage]`, defaulting to `usage`:

```
Ollama Cloud 用量：
  会话（5h） ▕█░░░░░░░░░▏ 已用 7.2% · 3 小时后重置
  每周（7d） ▕█░░░░░░░░░▏ 已用 6.4% · 18 小时后重置
  5h 统计：267 次请求 · 输入 8.9k · 输出 127
  7d 统计：1.2k 次请求 · 输入 8.9k · 输出 127
```

The settings page and the sidebar use these routes over the same origin; scripts can too.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/_dsh/ollama-cloud/status` | key configured?, route, model count, last sync |
| `GET` | `/_dsh/ollama-cloud/usage[?force=1]` | balance windows, usage, token totals |
| `POST` | `/_dsh/ollama-cloud/key` | `{ "key": "…" }` stores and syncs, `{ "remove": true }` deletes |
| `POST` | `/_dsh/ollama-cloud/sync` | re-pull the catalog |

`/key` and `/sync` write. They take the app's own page only (same origin, or an opaque `file://`
origin) and a loopback or IP-literal `Host`; everything else gets 403.

## Runtime compatibility

| Runtime | Settings seam | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `0.1.0-rc.x` | `ctx.settings.register` / `get` | the plugin owns the `ollama-cloud` section; the adapter's section is read with `get('llm-pi-ai')` |
| `0.2.x` (desktop) | `describe` / `mutate` | the entry config is the section; the adapter's entry is read with `describe()` and written with `mutate()` |

`engines.dsh` accepts `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <1.0.0`, so both runtimes load the bundle. Tested on
`0.1.0-rc.6` (CLI) and `0.2.1-rc.2` (the desktop app's bundled runtime). CSS tokens carry literal
fallbacks, so the older runtime renders the same layout with plainer colors.

## Known limits

There is no way to cap output from here. pi-ai's compatibility probe sends `max_completion_tokens`,
which Ollama ignores (it honors `max_tokens`), and `dsh-llm-pi-ai` exposes no switch for that field.

The local meter only sees traffic from this harness home. Another machine or another client will not
appear in the token totals, and hourly buckets can put a window edge off by up to an hour.

When the catalog changes, the sync replaces `llm-pi-ai.providers.ollama-cloud` whole, so any hand
edits to that route are lost. `syncOnStart: false` makes syncing a manual step.

`webTools` and `includeNonToolModels` are read when the tools register, so changing them needs a
restart. Client-side changes also need one.

The usage endpoint allows 10 requests per minute per user. One refresh is three calls, which is why
the result is cached and the sidebar polls every five minutes.

## Development

```sh
node test/smoke.mjs   # catalog mapping, thinking levels, usage math, meter, route guards
```

No build step. The host half is plain ESM; the client half is written in the loader's factory form
(`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`).

To run the web profile on the desktop app's bundled runtime:

```sh
APP="/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/MacOS/DeepSeek Harness"
CLI="$APP/../Resources/app.asar/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop-host/lib/cli.js"
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 DSH_HOME=/tmp/probe "$APP" --expose-internals "$CLI" --profile web --port 8130 --no-open
```

License: MIT.

# dsh-plugin-gmt

DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件：图形化使用固美特 **gmtMcp** 云端 ERP 能力。

## 能力

## 快速安装

见 [docs/安装到DSH操作说明.md](docs/安装到DSH操作说明.md)。

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-mcp-connector
```

安装后**重启 DSH**，打开「固美特ERP」→ 设置里填写云端 MCP → 测试连接 → 导出 JSON 到 MCP 连接器。

## 开发

```bash
npm run lint

node scripts/sync-catalog.mjs ../python/gmtMcp/app/erp/queries.py
```

- ERP 令牌只写入本机 `~/.dsh/storages/gmt-erp/mcp-secrets.json`

plugins.description: 面向 DeepSeek Harness 的 Claude Code 风格终端界面，支持 Windows、macOS 与 Linux，兼容透明终端、VS Code 主题和自定义配色。
plugins.readme_text:
> **Release compatibility:** The current tested Host is official `0.2.0-rc.2`. SeekTTY `1.3.0` is paired with that Host. See the [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md) for changes and installation, and the [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md) for exact package evidence.

SeekTTY

A terminal workspace for DeepSeek Harness.

Overview · Quick start · Clarify and Plan · Features · Compatibility

English · 中文

--- ## Overview Run `deepseek` from a project directory to use the native Agent, Session, model, permission, Settings, Profile, plugin, and persistence services of [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) in one terminal workspace. SeekTTY is the terminal surface; Harness remains the owner of runtime state. Models, Providers, Agent Presets, permissions, commands, tools, Settings, Skills, MCP servers, and marketplace sources are discovered from the running Harness. Capabilities added by upstream or third-party Bundles therefore appear without being hard-coded into SeekTTY. For requirements that still need definition, the optional [Clarify Host plugin](https://github.com/Hilbert-beinghappy/dsh-plugin-clarify) adds a guided `/clarify` workflow. It asks focused questions, updates a reviewable Draft after each answer, and returns the accepted Draft to the composer. Harness-native `/plan` can then turn the submitted requirement into an implementation plan. ## Development checkout Build and install a local SeekTTY package from the repository root: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm run build pnpm pack dsh plugin --profile tui add --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false ./seektty-1.3.0.tgz dsh --profile tui ``` Use the local tarball for source development and testing. For the released package, use the exact npm version below. ## Quick start Install the published SeekTTY release on its verified official DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 dsh plugin --profile tui add --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false seektty@1.3.0 dsh --profile tui ``` These commands install the prebuilt Bundle through native `dsh plugin` reconciliation. The per-command pnpm option avoids the pnpm 11 Global Virtual Store layout that the Cordis loader in the currently tested dsh releases cannot reliably load. SeekTTY never changes global pnpm configuration. Clarify and Auxiliary Runtime are optional, not default dependencies; their historical joint acceptance is listed under [Compatibility](#compatibility-and-verification). The exact `seektty@1.3.0` npm package is documented in the [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### Bare `deepseek` launcher After installing `dsh`, install the same SeekTTY release globally and pin Profile reconciliation to its exact npm version: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false seektty@1.3.0 export SEEKTTY_SPEC=seektty@1.3.0 deepseek ``` PowerShell uses the same exact npm spec: ```powershell pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false 'seektty@1.3.0' $env:SEEKTTY_SPEC='seektty@1.3.0' deepseek ``` `deepseek` requires `dsh` on `PATH`, or `DSH_BIN` pointing to its executable. Common launch forms include: ```sh deepseek "check this project" deepseek --cwd ../project deepseek --resume deepseek --resume deepseek --profile team-tui deepseek --version deepseek --update ``` `deepseek --update` is self-first: it checks SeekTTY before dsh, installs at most one compatible component per run, and never installs an untested gap or future Host. `DSH_BIN`, local installs, and `SEEKTTY_SPEC` overrides are left unchanged. Update failures do not block startup. Set `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=check` for a post-session notice or `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=0` to disable checks. SeekTTY `1.3.0` supports official dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` and brings more native workflows into the terminal. See the bilingual [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [complete PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### What's new in 1.3.0 - Access native Session actions, plans and artifacts, MCP resources, Team information, schedules, timed/continued questions, and account/model information from the terminal. - Browse Host workspace files with text/binary views and available file watching. Plugins can add terminal Session actions and guarded draft input activities with undo. - Install optional Creator, Browser, or Computer companion Bundles when you need them. With the official voice-input Bundle enabled, `/speech wav` provides reviewed WAV transcription; it does not record from the microphone. - Fix current-Host preset/forms/tool-result handling, stale targets, approval display, watcher cleanup, and bounded shutdown. Keep native Harness ownership and the existing terminal workflows. The release notes also fill gaps in the `1.2.6` summary: Agent Tree navigation, semantic transcript copying, target-specific context menus, Provider configuration, VS Code theme discovery, independent appearance controls, native scrollback, and long-session rendering fixes. Those features were already shipped; the [audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md) identifies their original PRs and versions. ## Interface | DeepSeek light | DeepSeek dark | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek light start screen](assets/seektty-tui.png) | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek dark start screen](assets/seektty-tui-dark.png) | | TypeScript in the light interface | Tools, file reads, and Diff in the dark interface | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY light TypeScript syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-light.png) | ![SeekTTY dark tool and Diff syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-dark.png) | Full mode uses a fixed alternate-screen viewport and keeps the composer and status at the bottom. Its mouse support browses history, selects text, and clicks existing controls inside SeekTTY. F3 or `/mouse native` switches while idle to terminal-native mode: SeekTTY leaves the alternate screen, writes the complete loaded conversation to ordinary terminal scrollback, disables mouse reporting, and lets the terminal or tmux own scrolling, search, and selection. Backfill is sequential and reports progress; Esc stops it without stopping the Session, while Ctrl+L refreshes only the active tail. `/transcript` opens transcript browsing and `/transcript replay` explicitly writes the available conversation again. Images use a textual attachment row in native mode. Already-written history is not recolored or reflowed by SeekTTY; the terminal owns that history. An empty session now opens with a responsive Fastfetch-style welcome page rather than sendable task suggestions. The default uses a packaged, original-color DeepSeek pixel whale plus runtime facts from the current Profile; it does **not** execute Fastfetch. The first-time API-key prompt remains higher priority and finishes before option

plugins.description: Permanent session removal for DeepSeek Harness. Adds Delete session... to the sidebar and removes the log, projection cache, and workspace accounting instead of archiving. Community plugin, not official.
plugins.readme_text:
**Archive hides a conversation. Delete removes it.** COMMUNITY PLUGIN  ·  NOT OFFICIAL  ·  MIT  ·  DSH 0.2.x

[Install](#install)  ·  [Use](#use)  ·  [How it works](#how-it-works)  ·  [Safety](#safety-model)  ·  [FAQ](#faq)

> **This is a community plugin, not an official DeepSeek product.** > > Session Delete is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed > by, or supported by DeepSeek AI, and it is not part of DeepSeek Harness. > DeepSeek Harness and DeepSeek are names and marks of their respective owners. > You are installing code that deletes files on purpose. Read > [Safety](#safety-model) first. ## Why this exists DeepSeek Harness archives sessions. Archiving is useful — the row leaves the sidebar, the session can come back — but it is not removal. The compressed log stays under `~/.dsh/sessions/`, the projection checkpoint stays under `~/.dsh/storages/session_projcache/`, and the workspace keeps accounting for an id you may never open again. Session Delete adds the missing verb. | | Archive | Delete | | --- | --- | --- | | Row leaves the sidebar | ✅ | ✅ | | Conversation log on disk | stays forever | **removed** | | Projection cache | stays | **removed** | | Workspace accounting / pin / archive entry | kept | **removed** | | Can be restored | unarchive | no | Archive is untouched. Delete is a second, explicit choice at the bottom of the same menu, behind a confirmation.

The new entry sits after the shipped actions, behind a hairline.
## Install **Requires [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 0.2.x** (tested on `0.2.1-rc.1`). Desktop and the Web UI are both supported. The repository is the install unit. The npm package inside it is `dsh-plugin-session-delete`; the spec you paste is the GitHub address. ### 1. From the Plugins page (recommended) 1. Open the sidebar and choose **Plugins**. 2. Install a plugin and paste: ```text github:Adolanium/dsh-session-delete ``` 3. Install it. The bundle is enabled by default. 4. Refresh the DeepSeek Harness window (`Ctrl+R` / `Cmd+R`). The browser half is loaded lazily, so the menu entry appears after a reload. No build permission is needed: the package ships plain JavaScript, has no `prepare` script, and has no runtime dependencies. ### 2. With the `dsh` CLI If you boot profiles yourself (Web, headless, or a stopped Desktop), the same spec installs into a named profile: ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Adolanium/dsh-session-delete ``` `dsh` appends the bundle to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` because the package declares `dsh.bundle`. Start DeepSeek Harness afterwards, then refresh the window. Pin the install if you want it frozen to this release: ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Adolanium/dsh-session-delete#v0.1.0 ``` Remove it with: ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-plugin-session-delete ``` > Running the CLI against the `desktop` profile while the Desktop app is running > is supported by the profile lock, but the Plugins page is the smoother path > there — it owns the same operation and reports activation status. ### 3. From a checkout (development) ```powershell git clone https://github.com/Adolanium/dsh-session-delete.git cd dsh-session-delete pwsh -File scripts/install-dev.ps1 ``` That links the checkout into `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules` and adds the Loader entry to the profile patch (with a timestamped backup). Undo with `scripts/uninstall-dev.ps1`. > The profile reloads configuration live, so a linked package activates without > a restart. HMR does not watch module roots, so **code edits need a restart**. ## Use Open a session row's **⋯** menu and choose **Delete session…**. The dialog names the conversation and explains that the log and its cached projections will be removed. **Delete** performs the removal; **Cancel** leaves everything alone. What happens next depends on the session: | Session state | Result | | --- | --- | | **Cold** — no live Agent owns it | Removed immediately. The row leaves the list; the dialog closes. | | **Live** — open in this app, or a running turn owns it | The dialog explains that the log is still in use and offers **Delete on next start**. | | **Unknown id** | Rejected. Nothing is touched. | ### Delete on next start A live session cannot be pulled out from under its Agent, so the second option queues it instead: - the id is written to `~/.dsh/plugin-session-delete/pending.json`; - the session is archived (best effort) so the row disappears from the default list; - the next DeepSeek Harness start retries the removal, when the write handle is free; - **unarchiving the session cancels its queued removal** — the archive is the visible "pending removal" state. A queued id whose session is already gone is dropped silently. A queued id that is still in use stays queued for the next start. ## What Delete removes For one session id, the Host removes: - **the session directory** under `~/.dsh/sessions///`, including every format generation (`session.vN.jsonl.zstd`) and the lock artifact; - **the projection-cache record** from the `session_projcache` domain, through the domain itself, so an in-memory row cannot survive the delete; - **the workspace accounting slot**, the global pin, and the archive entry. It deliberately leaves: - **attachments** — content-addressed under `~/.dsh/attachments` and possibly shared with other sessions; - **subagent child sessions** — separate ids, hidden from the sidebar by design; delete them individually; - **the SQLite search index**, if your composition uses `dsh-session-query-sqlite` — it reconciles deleted sources on the next search; - **derived rows in other domains** (telemetry, titles) — they are keyed by an id that no longer resolves and are ignored. ## Safety model Deleting a file is easy. Deleting the *right* file while the app is running is the hard part. The plugin is built around four rules: 1. **One writer.** Before touching anything, the Host takes the persistence **write handle** for the session and immediately closes it. A live Agent, another DSH process, or a crashed-but-held lock makes that open fail, and the delete is refused. The handle is the proof of "nobody is using this". 2. **Loopback only.** The route is rejected for non-loopback peers. A present `Origin` must be the Web client's origin or the Desktop shell's `dsh-app://app`; a cross-site `fetch` cannot reach it (JSON content type forces a preflight the route does not answer). 3. **Strict identity.** The id must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`, the target directory must be named exactly that id, and it must contain a canonical `session[.vN].jsonl[.zstd]` log. A malformed id cannot address another path. 4. **No surprises.** If the materialized log is not under the configured root, the Host refuses and says so instead of deleting accounting and leaving the log behind. Cleanup failures are logged; the response reports what happened. There is no network access, no telemetry, and no background process. The plugin reads and writes local files through the Host's own services. ## Configuration All fields are optional. Defaults match a stock installation. | Field | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `dshHome` | `$DSH_HOME`, else `~/.dsh` | Data root used to derive the two roots below. | | `sessionsRoot` | `/sessions` | Session persistence root — the `root` of `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`. | | `storagesRoot` | `/storages` | Storage root used only as a fallback when the `storageDomain` service is absent. | Set these in the profile entry if you run a non-default persistence root: ```yaml - id: session-de

plugins.description: WeChat bridge + phone layout for DeepSeek Harness: chat with your DSH from WeChat (text, images, files, daily digest) and use its web UI on a phone. 微信桥接 + 手机端适配，把 DeepSeek Harness 变成随身可用的 AI 助手
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-phone-bridge **Turn [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) into something you can carry in your pocket** — a WeChat bot that talks to your DSH from anywhere, plus a plugin that reshapes the DSH web UI into a phone-shaped app. [中文说明](README.zh-CN.md) · [Setup guide](docs/SETUP.md) · [**Phone app**](docs/MOBILE-APP.md) · [Pitfalls](docs/PITFALLS.md) · [**Usage boundary**](docs/USAGE-BOUNDARY.md) > ⚠️ **Personal use only.** This is a single-owner tool: one person, one bot, one conversation. It is **not** authorised for public services, group messaging, marketing, harassment, privacy invasion, circumventing platform rules, or operating someone else's account — see [docs/USAGE-BOUNDARY.md](docs/USAGE-BOUNDARY.md). You are solely responsible for how you deploy it.

  

## What's inside Two independent DSH plugins — use either one on its own. ### 1. `dsh-wechat-connect` — WeChat bridge Runs on your server and long-polls the WeChat iLink bot gateway. Text, images, voice and files go both ways, in **one single conversation** with **one single working directory** — the bot serves its owner and nobody else. - **Send the bot a photo** → DSH reads it with vision tools. **Send a document** → DSH opens it. - **Ask for a file** → the model writes `[[send:/abs/path]]` and the bridge uploads it back to the chat. - **Scheduled digest** — at a configured time every day, DSH researches the previous day's world + AI news and pushes it as **both** a chat message and a Word document. - **Self-healing** — the long-poll loop rebuilds itself after any failure, and writes a heartbeat so an external watchdog can catch the "process alive but wedged" case. ### 2. `dsh-mobile-ui` — phone layout for the DSH web UI The shipped web surface is a three-column desktop layout; on a phone the composer hides behind the keyboard, the sidebar crushes the conversation to a sliver, and the settings page wraps every label one character per line. This plugin injects a stylesheet plus a small script through the documented `webserver/index-inject` seam — **no source edits, no dist patching**: | Problem on a phone | What the plugin does | |---|---| | Left icon rail eats 56px, controls are 28px tall | Bottom tab bar, 44px touch targets | | Keyboard covers the composer | Layout height tracks `visualViewport` | | Sidebar squeezes content to 132px | Full-screen conversation drawer that auto-closes on pick | | Settings crushes labels vertically | Full-screen single column, nav becomes a horizontal strip | | Right sidebar opens with no way back | A visible "← back to chat" button | | iOS zooms the page on focus | 16px inputs | | No home-screen app | PWA manifest + PNG icons → **installs as an app** (own icon, full screen, no browser UI) | > 📱 **It also becomes a real phone app** — no APK, no app store: Chrome → "Add to Home screen" gives you a full-screen app icon, and the manifest's `start_url` can point at a short login link so it re-authenticates itself. See [docs/MOBILE-APP.md](docs/MOBILE-APP.md). ## Repository layout ``` packages/ dsh-wechat-connect/ WeChat bridge plugin (iLink gateway) dsh-mobile-ui/ Phone layout plugin (HTTP injection, no source edits) deploy/ systemd/ boot start, crash restart, watchdog, session filing, journald caps scripts/ watchdog + workspace-filing scripts nginx/ reverse proxy + mTLS device-level access example pwa/ manifest example + icon renderer (home-screen app) docs/ SETUP.md zero-to-running deployment guide MOBILE-APP.md installing the web UI as a phone app (PWA) PITFALLS.md 18 hard-won lessons about DSH internals and the WeChat gateway USAGE-BOUNDARY.md personal-use-only terms ``` ## Quick start ```bash # Server with Node 20+ npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh # Drop the plugins into a DSH profile and list them in its bundles — see docs/SETUP.md ``` Minimal profile config (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/wechat/cordis.patch.yml`): ```yaml - id: wechat-connect config: enabled: true sessionProfile: headless workDir: /root/dsh-convos/wechat # one working directory, one session allowFrom: "wxid_your_peer@im.wechat" # your own id only; empty or "*" = anyone schedule: enabled: true time: "06:00" prompt: | [scheduled digest] Research yesterday's world + AI news, write a Word document, summarise it as a chat message, then output [[send:/abs/path]]. ``` Full walkthrough — model API, QR login, reverse proxy with client certificates, keep-alive stack: **[docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md)**. ## Design notes - **Single owner, single conversation.** The bridge keeps one working directory and one DSH session — the shape the WeChat bot gateway is actually built around. No per-contact machinery to misconfigure. - **No DSH forks or patches.** The phone layout rides the documented index-injection seam; the bridge is a plain DSH plugin. - **Clone, don't move.** When the plugin needs a button in a React-owned subtree (bottom tabs, composer actions), it clones the original node and forwards clicks — React reconciliation is never disturbed. - **Three layers of keep-alive.** systemd restart on crash → in-plugin loop rebuild on failure → external heartbeat watchdog for the wedged-but-alive case. ## Known limits - The bot is a **separate WeChat account**, not you: it only sees messages sent *to it*, and cannot read your personal chats. - It is built for one owner. Keep `allowFrom` set to your own WeChat id so strangers who find the bot get ignored. - Proactive pushes (the digest) need a `context_token` from an inbound message, so you must message the bot once first. - The iLink bot gateway is not a public, versioned API; `channel_version` changes the upload response shape (the code handles both). ## License and usage boundary MIT for the code. Usage is limited to **personal self-hosted use** — see [docs/USAGE-BOUNDARY.md](docs/USAGE-BOUNDARY.md).

plugins.description: Time-shifting task delegation for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): plan tasks at leisure, they run unattended off-peak, come back to a report. Human-adjudicated, desktop + web.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-lowtide **Queue tasks when it's busy. They run on their own when it's cheap.** Semi-auto or full-auto, off the model's peak hours and peak prices. A must-have plugin for DeepSeek Harness. **English** | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [繁體中文](./README.zh-HK.md) | [العربية](./docs/README.ar.md) | [Deutsch](./docs/README.de.md) | [Español](./docs/README.es.md) | [Français](./docs/README.fr.md) | [Italiano](./docs/README.it.md) | [한국어](./docs/README.ko.md)
--- ![hero](./assets/screenshots/hero.png)

Three tasks waiting in the queue, the price status glowing in the session header, auto-run when your window opens

## Introduction lowtide is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh). The problem it solves is plain and perfectly natural: Usually, when you want an agent to do some work, you sit at the computer, send the agent an instruction, wait for the reply, and then review it by hand. But this workflow seems to forget that you have plenty of idle time — and a chance to dodge the peak/off-peak pricing that some models charge. With lowtide installed, the day goes like this: whenever a job crosses your mind during the day, toss it in the queue, glance at it, release it. The tasks pile up until the time you set (say, after 7 PM — that's when DeepSeek is at valley pricing), then run by themselves. Next morning you open the report: keep what went well, send back what didn't. That's all it is. But use it for a week and your working rhythm genuinely slows down — and don't forget, "time is money, efficiency is life"... A few key capabilities: - Four execution strategies: single, iterative, sampling, review — from "one pass is enough" to "run five candidates and I'll pick" - 168 unit tests + 10 end-to-end specs, CI green across ubuntu / windows × node 22 / 24 - One build artifact serves both desktop and web — install once, works on both - Off-peak execution lands in DeepSeek's valley hours: the same batch costs about half of what peak would ## A normal day with an agent might look like this… **Ten minutes before clocking out.** You've finished reviewing code, so you file three tickets for tomorrow: a refactor (iterative, 3 rounds), a weekly report (single), and a design you're unsure about (sampling, 4 candidates). Release them all, shut down, leave. Tomorrow at your desk, the morning report says: the refactor's done, the report's drafted, and four candidate designs sit side by side, each with its cost written out. **Friday night.** Queue a week's worth of chores in one go: dependency cleanup, missing tests, data scripts. Weekends are valley price around the clock. You go out; it works from home. Monday you check the report — retry what failed, merge what's good. **A 10 AM brainwave.** You're mid-conversation with the agent about an urgent bug when you think "hey, update the docs too." The intercept card pops up: running now costs peak price, tonight it's about half — the difference is spelled out. Click "queue for off-peak"; your draft survives untouched, and you go back to the bug. **An always-on server.** You've got a machine running dsh 24/7. Switch to L3 full-auto, then file tasks from anywhere through the API (`POST /ds-lowtide/tasks`). It runs them on schedule and writes the report. Nobody's watching, but the sandbox, the daily budget, and the file locks are all still there. **Deliverables for a client.** Use the review strategy: run once, then automatically open an independent session that tears the result apart through your chosen focus (say, "hunt for data-source errors"). In the morning you don't get a bare result — you get a result plus a critical review. **Living abroad.** You're in San Francisco; DeepSeek's peak is Beijing time, which for you lands in the evening and night before. Settings converts the official hours to your local clock, one click to adopt. You set windows by your own schedule, and the books always stay aligned with the official table. ## How lowtide works ``` ① Intake ② Adjudicate ③ Execute ④ Accept Whenever you have The queue dock When the off-peak When you're back: a moment: one-click groups tasks by window opens: five open the report — from the intercept workspace; triage preflight gates pass, results + diff card, or file a → line by line: → then sandboxed runs → + actual spend ticket (4 strategies) ✓approve ⏸defer one batch per window + money saved ✕drop / approve-all ``` A task's life: `pending-review → queued → preflight → running → done / failed / stale / timeout`, plus `deferred` (postponed) and `dropped` (soft-deleted, restorable). Step two is where lowtide differs from a "fully automated script": **every task must be released by your hand before it runs** (in L2, you release the whole batch at once, 30 minutes before the window). The machine cannot move itself into the run queue. Execution is automated; decisions are not. That's why you can safely be absent. ## A tour of the lowtide interface **The new-task modal.** Four strategies side by side, each with a plain-language hint; rounds, priority, and run mode ride along per task — no trip back to settings. Tasks land as "pending review". Nothing enters the queue without passing you. ![new-task-modal](./assets/screenshots/new-task-modal.png) **Advanced options.** Model, reasoning effort, priority from 0 to 9, fresh session or continue-previous, and the locked-files list — all in one small pane. Locked files, briefly: anything on the list gets sha256-checked before execution, and if it doesn't match what you filed, the task goes stale and refuses to run. Otherwise the file you queued against could be rewritten by another task while waiting, and this one would blindly stomp on it. ![advanced-options](./assets/screenshots/advanced-options.png) **Pick any model.** Batch runs default to the official `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the retired `deepseek-v4-flash` name still routes there at Flash prices), but each task can pick its own model — anything connected to your Harness is in the dropdown, grouped by provider. Private providers work too. Non-official models have no public price table, so the ledger honestly says "price unknown"; add a price override in settings if you want the bookkeeping exact. ![model-picker](./assets/screenshots/model-picker.png) **The window editor.** Multi-segment, overnight, per-weekday — all fine. Underneath is a live 24-hour price band: red for peak, green for valley, and a marker showing where you are right now. Outside UTC+8, one click on "adopt official peak hours" converts Beijing time to your local clock. ![window-editor](./assets/screenshots/window-editor.png) **The settings page.** Window hours, tasks per batch, per-task duration cap, concurrency, daily budget, report history, autonomy level, price overrides — all graphical, no config files. The official pricing rules (including the new all-weekend valley) are explained in human language on the same page. ![settings](./assets/screenshots/settings.png) Three more pieces of UI appear in daily use: the **price pill** (session header — busy/idle, queue size; click it to edit windows), the **peak-hours intercept card** (type at peak, it appears; the price difference is spelled out; your draft survives), and the **execution report** (the morning briefing: savings first, anomalies pinned, candidates awaiting your pick, one-click Markdown copy). ## About lowtide workspaces Every task runs inside a workspace. That single dropdown decides three things. **Which files it can touch.** Tasks run in a sandbox whose boundary is the workspace directory. Pick wrong and at best it can't find the files; at worst it edits something it shouldn't. **Who it queues with.** Tasks in the same workspace run serially (two tasks never fight over one repo); different workspaces run in paralle

plugins.description: Windows / DSH 环境医生：体检 + 可执行修复
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-env-doctor

> Windows / DSH 环境医生 —— 说一句「体检一下」，拿到「哪里坏了 + 为什么 + 该敲什么」。

**状态：v0.1.0 已发布到 npm。** 设计文档仍在（[检查目录](docs/checks/catalog.md)、[安全模型](docs/safety/model.md)、[报告格式](docs/prototypes/report/)），随包一起发。

[中文](#dsh-env-doctor) · [English](#english)

---

## 1. 它解决什么

Windows 上跑 DSH（或任何 Node 工具链），坏掉的方式往往很隐蔽：命令明明装了却解析到 `.ps1`、`git push` 卡在凭据、`bash` 起不来但不是 Git 坏了、沙箱把写入拒了却给不出原因。这些问题的共同点是——**报错信息不指向真正的原因**。

`dsh-env-doctor` 做一件事：把该查的都查一遍，按「真的坏了 / 能用但要注意 / 说不准」三档给结论，每条都带原始证据和可以直接粘贴的命令。

它不是万能修复器，设计上刻意保守：

- **体检零副作用**：除了两个自写自删的探针文件，不建文件、不改配置、不动注册表。
- **只有 4 条能自动修**（`B.2` / `C.4` / `D.1` / `E.3`），且都要你先明确点头；其余只给命令。
- **说不准就说不准**：探测不到时给 `undiagnosed` 并说明原因，绝不猜成 `ok`。

## 2. 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-env-doctor
```

装完**完全退出** DSH Desktop 再打开一次（模块代码要重启才加载；只热更新配置不够）。`dsh web` 用户用 `--profile web` 并重启 `dsh web`。

> 装不上时优先试：`add dsh-env-doctor@latest --registry https://registry.npmjs.org`。刚发布的版本可能被 pnpm 的 `minimumReleaseAge` 供应链接管期静默跳过，或镜像还没同步。

## 3. 使用

在对话里说「**体检一下**」，或直接点名工具：

```
dsh_env_doctor(mode="check")
```

三种模式：

| 模式 | 做什么 | 写东西吗 |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | 跑全部 17 项，写报告文件 | 只写报告（默认在你工作区的 `.dsh-doctor/`） |
| `explain` | 不跑命令，按当前沙箱模式解释某一项为什么这样判 | 不写 |
| `fix` | 执行一条已确认的修复（见第 5 节） | 会改你点头的那一处 |

报告写到 `<工作区>/.dsh-doctor/report-<时间戳>.md`（旁边一份同内容 JSON 供历史对比），给模型看的只有十来行摘要。

## 4. 它检查什么（17 项）

| 组 | 查什么 | 项 |
|---|---|---|
| **A** 沙箱与文件权限 | 沙箱模式、工作区可写性、边界是否生效、ACL 是否被改坏 | A.1–A.3 |
| **B** Git Bash | 能不能启动（沙箱内启动失败是已知限制，判 `undiagnosed` 而不是故障）、是否在 PATH | B.1–B.2 |
| **C** 网络 / TLS / 凭据 | npm registry 可达性、TLS 栈、代理三处一致性、git 凭据助手是否指向不存在的程序 | C.1–C.4 |
| **D** 执行策略 | PowerShell 是否拦住 `npm.ps1` / `pnpm.ps1` | D.1 |
| **E** 工具链 | DSH 与 Node 版本、必备命令、同名多份安装、pnpm 大版本、python | E.1–E.5 |
| **F** 权限与安装通道 | 管理员/winget/choco/scoop、磁盘空间与长路径 | F.1–F.2 |

完整的判据、探测命令、危险等级在 [检查目录](docs/checks/catalog.md)；那份表是实现和历史的唯一契约，id 发布后不再改。

## 5. 它会改什么、绝不改什么

**能自动修的 4 条**（都要你先确认，命令逐字打印，旧值记进报告以便撤销）：

| id | 改什么 |
|---|---|
| `B.2` | 把 bash 所在目录追加进**用户级** PATH |
| `C.4` | 删掉指向不存在程序的 git 凭据 helper，再 `gh auth setup-git` |
| `D.1` | 把 `CurrentUser` 执行策略设为 `RemoteSigned` |
| `E.3` | 调整**用户级** PATH 顺序，让 `.cmd` 优先于 `.ps1` |

**永不碰**：ACL（交棒内置技能 `diagnose-windows-sandbox-acl`）、注册表安全项、MSI/需要 UAC 的安装、系统级 PATH、任何带密码或令牌的文件。这些一律只给命令。

安全模型的完整论证（为什么"体检不写"能靠代码保证、两道确认门在哪、怎么测）见 [docs/safety/model.md](docs/safety/model.md)。

## 6. 报告长什么样

给模型的摘要（十来行，不是报告全文）：

```
体检完成：17 项检查 —— 通过 13、注意 2、失败 1、说不准 1。总体：失败
1. [高危] C.4 git 凭据助手指向的程序是否存在
   → git config --global --unset-all credential.https://github.com.helper
2. [中] D.1 执行策略是否拦 `.ps1` 脚本
   → Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned
3. [低] E.3 同名命令多份安装 / 解析到意料之外
   → 把 %APPDATA%\npm 与 pnpm 的 .cmd shim 所在目录在用户级 PATH 中前置到 WindowsApps 之前
说不准：B.1（原因见报告）
全文：C:\...\.dsh-doctor\report-20261014-171203.md
```

这段就是 [sample-summary.md](docs/prototypes/report/sample-summary.md) 的原文（那个示例里 `B.2` 已经修完并复检通过，所以它不在「要动手」里，而是出现在报告的「已执行的修复」）。

完整报告是 Markdown：顶部一张元信息表 + 一句话结论，然后每个问题一节（现象 / 证据 / 下一步），最后是 17 项总表和「说不准的」。样例见 [docs/prototypes/report/sample-report.md](docs/prototypes/report/sample-report.md)（**构造的示例**，用来演示四种 verdict 的形状，不是某台机器的真体检记录）。

## 7. 常见问题

- **`B.1` 说 bash 起不来，可我明明能用 Git Bash？** 在 DSH 沙箱里启动 MSYS2 会报 `couldn't create signal pipe, Win32 error 5`，这是沙箱限制，不是你的 Git 坏了——所以判 `undiagnosed` 并给你一条在新终端里跑的命令。
- **`A.3` 为什么总是「说不准」？** ACL 的真损坏只有两类（授权树里缺有效的 `WRITE_DAC`/`WRITE_OWNER`，或出现显式 AppContainer 包 ACE）；其余一律不猜。这项交棒给内置技能处理，本插件不改 ACL。
- **报告的 id 会变吗？** 不会。`C.4` 这类 id 是历史对比的键，只许往后追加新项。

## 8. 卸载

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-env-doctor
```

自动修过的东西不会自动还原——按报告里每条的「撤销」命令回退即可。

## 9. 开发

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ZJYSZT/dsh-env-doctor
cd dsh-env-doctor
npm test                      # 假 shell 的单元测试 + 四组安全测试（见 docs/safety/model.md §4）
npm run test:e2e              # 在本机真跑 17 项（会真的读注册表 / 查 PATH，不写除报告外的任何东西）
npm run verify:samples        # 重新生成报告样例并验证 schema / 样例 / 渲染器三者不漂移
dsh plugin --profile desktop add .    # 本地装进 profile
```

发布流程（版本策略、registry 前置条件、发布清单）见 [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md)。

## 10. 许可

[Apache-2.0](LICENSE)，版权声明见 [NOTICE](NOTICE)。

---

## English

**dsh-env-doctor** is a Windows environment doctor for [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-harness). Say "run a health check" and get a verdict per check — *broken / worth noting / can't tell* — each with raw evidence and a command you can paste.

Design principles: the health check never mutates your machine (only a report file), exactly four items can be auto-fixed (`B.2`, `C.4`, `D.1`, `E.3`) and only after you explicitly confirm, and anything unobservable is reported as `undiagnosed` instead of being guessed as `ok`.

**Status:** design complete, implementation in progress; `v0.1.0` is not published yet.

**Install (once published):**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-env-doctor
# then fully quit and reopen DSH Desktop
```

**Use:**

```
dsh_env_doctor(mode="check")     # run all 17 checks, write the report
dsh_env_doctor(mode="explain", input="A.3")   # explain one check without running it
dsh_env_doctor(mode="fix", fix={id:"C.4", confirm:true})   # one confirmed fix
```

Reports go to `<workspace>/.dsh-doctor/report-<timestamp>.md` plus a JSON twin for history. The 17 checks cover sandbox/ACL, Git Bash, network/TLS/credentials, PowerShell execution policy, toolchain, and install channels. Never touched: ACLs, registry security keys, anything needing UAC, system PATH, credential files.

Full design — check catalog, safety model, report schema — lives in [`docs/`](docs/). Licensed under [Apache-2.0](LICENSE).

plugins.description: A portable memory protocol for AI agents — load it as standing rules; a curation discipline + reference spec + optional cap hook.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# Engramory

[![CI](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

**An opinionated, zero-infrastructure memory *protocol* for small-scale, local,
file-based agent memory** — a strict curation discipline plus a validator
(`tools/engramory_doctor.py`), loaded as **standing rules** (`CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` / your host's rules file). It is not a database, a framework, or a
relevance-loaded skill. Memory is a folder of small, human-readable markdown files
plus one always-loaded index. No database, no embeddings, no server — just
plain-text files you can open, read, edit, and diff in any editor (the live store
itself stays git-ignored).

> *Engramory* — coined from *engram* (the physical trace a memory leaves in the
> brain) + *memory*. Here: one file = one fact.

> ⚠️ **Unrelated projects share this name.** *engram + memory* is an obvious
> coinage and at least one other repository arrived at it independently. This
> project is only ever `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (npm: `dsh-engramory`); a same-named
> repo under a different owner is not a fork, a mirror, or a newer version of it.

> 🤖 **Are you an AI agent, asked to install or check this?** Start at
> **[AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md)**, not at the install steps below. It is the
> procedure for working out what your host can actually enforce, whether a store
> already exists, what you must not touch, and what to tell the user — the parts
> agents reliably get wrong when improvising.

> **Status: 0.12.1 — experimental.** The hard index cap (a `PreToolUse` hook) is
> deterministic for the matched direct-edit tools (`Edit | Write | MultiEdit`) but
> NOT a global write guard (shell tools — Bash, PowerShell, a background Monitor
> command — plus MCP file tools, external editors, and sync clients bypass it);
> the discipline loads as standing rules the model follows, so it's
> best-effort, not guaranteed on every task (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §8). Assumes a
> single writer / serialized writes. Don't rely on it as a "mandatory, reliable,
> cross-agent" memory layer yet.

---

## What this is — and is NOT

Engramory is **not a new memory architecture**. The "markdown files + a small index
loaded into context + the model curates it" pattern is now the mainstream shape
for agent memory, and it ships in several places already. Engramory stands on:
